name: Rear Hubs & Bearings
description: Driven rear corners: bolt-in hub bearing unit with splined bore; the halfshaft outer CV stub passes through and is retained by an axle (drive-shaft) nut.

components.name: Rear wheel bearing & hub assembly
components.description: Sealed, bolt-in rear hub bearing with splined center for the halfshaft and pressed M14x1.5 studs. Sees full drive torque and cornering loads on slicks – inspect every event, replace on a schedule.
components.location: Rear knuckle, each side, flange outboard at z≈±0.73–0.77.

factory.name: GM rear wheel bearing and hub assembly (Gen 6 Camaro)

raceOptions.name: New OEM GM/ACDelco or Timken/SKF unit each season

hardware.item: Rear wheel bearing and hub bolt
hardware.spec: M12 flange bolt (qty/size not confirmed – verify)
hardware.torqueSequence: Clean the old threadlocker off the threads and apply new threadlocker. Torque in a cross pattern to 130 N·m. No angle step is listed.
hardware.threadlocker: Clean threads; re-apply threadlocker per SKF/OE (verify GM spec)
hardware.notes: GM 2016–18 value via TightTorque. [2026-10 check] The SKF 2023 Torque Specification Guide gives 2016–21 Camaro rear hub mount at 96 ft-lb (130 N·m) with footnote [45] (new threadlocker), which matches TightTorque (GM 2016–18 SI). BMR BK065's 45 ft-lb for the same bolts conflicts and looks low. Note that the threadlocker field may say 'none', but SKF says to re-apply threadlocker.

installNotes: Clean knuckle face; install hub; torque bolts in a cross pattern.
Insert halfshaft splines (clean, light oil unless GM SI specifies dry/threadlocker), fit new axle nut.
inspection: Check play and noise each event; check for grease leaks at seals.

modelRef.dimensions: Flange face at z=0.808 (rotor hat 9 mm, wheel face 0.817); 5 x 120, 66.9 mm pilot; splined bore for the halfshaft
modelRef.features: Bolt-on driven hub: splined bore, axle nut recessed in the pilot

components.name: Rear axle (wheel drive shaft) nut & washer
components.description: Clamps the halfshaft CV stub to the hub bearing inner race, preloading the bearing. Under-torque here causes clicking/fretting and bearing failure.
components.location: Center of each rear hub, outboard face (behind the wheel center).

factory.name: GM rear wheel drive shaft nut

hardware.torque: 199 ft-lb (270 N·m) per GM 2016–18 SI listing; SKF lists 185 ft-lb (250 N·m). Unresolved, confirm in GM SI.
hardware.torqueSequence: Use a NEW nut. Torque with the rotor locked or the wheel on the ground, then stake the nut if required (SKF note [107]).
hardware.notes: TightTorque (GM-derived) lists 199 ft-lb / 270 N·m for 2016–2024 Camaro. [2026-10 check] DOWNGRADED from typical because the sources conflict. TightTorque (GM 2016–18 SI) gives 270 N·m. The SKF 2023 Torque Specification Guide gives 185/250 for 2016–21 Camaro, and also for the Alpha-sibling ATS and 2016–19 CTS, with footnote [107] (use a new nut and stake it as required). Owner posts that quote '199 ft-lb' mostly refer to the Gen 5 car. Get the GM SI value for your model year before final torque.

installNotes: Hold the hub with a long bar across two lug nuts (protect studs) or have an assistant on the brake; never use the impact gun for final torque.

sources.title: TightTorque – axle nut & wheel bearing torque chart (Camaro 2016–2024 rows)

modelRef.dimensions: 36 mm hex (approx.) inside the hub pilot bore
modelRef.features: Flanged hex nut + washer on the halfshaft stub
